clinician.final_diagnosis: Peripheral primitive neuroectodermal tumor (PNET/Ewing sarcoma) of the left kidney with 20% tumor necrosis
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 32-year-old Iranian female with no significant past medical history presented to Rajaei Hospital Cardiac Center in Tehran with progressive dyspnea at rest. Initial clinical suspicion of pulmonary embolism prompted anticoagulation therapy. Spiral CT imaging of the chest, mediastinum, abdomen, and pelvis revealed a large heterogeneously enhancing solid mass at the left kidney mid to lower pole (70 mm × 75 mm × 105 mm) with tumor thrombosis extending into the left renal vein and IVC superiorly over ~23 cm, terminating below the right atrium. Incidental findings included filling defects in the right main pulmonary artery and segmental branches consistent with pulmonary thromboembolism, and a 7 mm ground-glass nodule in the left lower lobe. Left radical nephrectomy was performed. Macroscopic examination revealed a 7 cm × 6.5 cm × 5 cm mass in the lower pole of the kidney with extension to the renal sinus. Microscopic examination showed sheet-like diffuse infiltration of small round neoplastic cells with monomorphic nuclei, fine speckled chromatin pattern, inconspicuous nucleoli, and occasional pseudorosette-like structures. Immunohistochemistry was positive for CD99, NKX2.2, synaptophysin, and chromogranin, and negative for CK7, CK20, CK, LCA, PAX8, AMACR, P63, CKA1/A3, and TLE1. FISH analysis identified EWSR1 gene rearrangement at (11;22) translocation, confirming the diagnosis of peripheral PNET/Ewing sarcoma. Postoperative course was uneventful with discharge 1 week after surgery. The patient initiated systemic chemotherapy 2 months postoperatively and remained on anticoagulant therapy due to prothrombotic risk from both malignancy and chemotherapy.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: While pulmonary emboli were confirmed on imaging, they were incidental findings. The primary pathology was the left renal mass with tumor thrombus, which explained the dyspnea and the thrombotic complications.

The immunohistochemistry panel was negative for PAX8 and AMACR, markers typically positive in RCC. The positive CD99 and NKX2.2, along with EWSR1 translocation, are diagnostic of PNET/Ewing sarcoma, not RCC.

While the tumor showed neuroendocrine features (positive synaptophysin and chromogranin), the EWSR1 (11;22) translocation and CD99/NKX2.2 positivity are specific for PNET/Ewing sarcoma rather than neuroblastoma.
